races.title: State House, District 49
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Cynthia Ball
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 49 (Wake County) since 2017. House Democratic Deputy Leader. Certified professional mediator with an MBA. Former director of development and external affairs programs at William Peace University and NC State University, and executive director of two NC State foundations.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. We could not read her list of sponsored bills, so no specific bill is cited. Her birth year and the year she moved to Raleigh were not found. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 100: She was born in Franklin County, NC, graduated from her public school in Franklinton, and has lived in Raleigh while serving in the legislature since 2017.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2017 and held caucus leadership roles: Freshman Democratic Chair, Democratic Whip, Democratic Conference Chair and now Deputy Leader. Earlier she did marketing research and directed development programs at two universities. She also served as executive director of two NC State foundations, holds an MBA, and works as a certified mediator.
qual.why: Nearly a decade of legislative service and caucus leadership, plus management and fundraising roles and an MBA, fit the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.
qual.label: Nearly a decade of legislative service and caucus leadership, plus management and fundraising roles and an MBA, fit the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says the state should not keep accelerating a voucher program for the wealthiest North Carolinians while public schools struggle. It also calls for fully funding public schools and supporting educators and staff.

cands.name: Daran Thomas
cands.bio: Daran Thomas was the Republican nominee for North Carolina House District 49 in 2026. The sources reviewed give no information on his occupation, background or any prior offices held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Daran Thomas was born or raised, when he moved to North Carolina, or what his career or work history is. He has held no office that we could find. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his own stated positions on the issues were not found. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, development, property taxes, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no endorsements, controversies or foreign ties. The only page available was a Ballotpedia election page, which lists no biography.
